title: How to use the worksheets
use: Orientation film for the worksheet workbook (On-Chain-Operator-Worksheets.xlsx). UI captured 2026-09-28 from a preview of that workbook. Facts last checked: 2026-09-28. Lesson 3.2 example: quantity 10, price 3000, liquidation threshold 0.80, debt 12000 prints health factor 2.00 and liquidation price $1,500. Lesson 12.1 example: collateral 300000, reserve 40000, loans 60000, borrow 5%, spend 5000 prints equity $280,000, LTV 20%, health factor 4.0, runway about 7.6 months. Lesson 13.3 example: five positions, $500,000, payout ratio 0.70 prints expected income $23,300 and payout $16,310. W4 examples score 4×5=20 and 3×5=15. All figures are lesson examples for learning, not a forecast. The workbook is not inside the directory zip.

scenes.title: How to use the worksheets
scenes.sub: Which sheet, when, and what you type.
scenes.vo: This is the worksheet workbook for the On-Chain Operator Program. In this film you will learn which sheet to open, when in the course you open it, and how a yellow cell becomes a green answer.

scenes.sub: A decision you do not write down is one you cannot review.
scenes.vo: A long course is easy to lose track of. The decision you do not write down is the one you cannot review. This file is where the lesson turns into a record.

scenes.title: What you will be able to do
scenes.vo: By the end you will be able to do four things. Open the workbook in a spreadsheet. Pick the sheet that matches the lesson you are on. Type in a yellow cell, and read the green answer. And keep secrets out of every sheet.

scenes.title: Where the number should live

left.label: A note, and then it goes stale
items: The health factor does not update
The risk score is not multiplied

right.label: Yellow in, green out
items: The green cell is the formula

scenes.vo: A note can hold a number, and then that number goes stale. The health factor does not update, and the risk score is not multiplied. The yellow cell is the one you type. The green cell is the course formula. And the credit policy on W eight reads the balance sheet, so the check stays tied to the numbers.
scenes.cap: A note can hold a number, and then that number goes stale. The health factor does not update, and the risk score is not multiplied. The yellow cell is the one you type. scenes.label: On screen: the health-factor tool
scenes.vo: On Tools, yellow means you type, and green means the sheet answers. The lesson three point two example is ten units at three thousand dollars, a threshold of point eight zero, and twelve thousand dollars of debt. The health factor reads two point zero zero. The liquidation price reads one thousand five hundred dollars. Those figures are the lesson example, for learning, not a forecast.
scenes.cap: On Tools, yellow means you type, and green means the sheet answers. The lesson 3.2 example is 10 units at $3,000, a threshold of 0.80, and $12,000 of debt. The health factor reads 2.00. The liquidation price reads $1,500. Those figures are the lesson example, for learning, not a forecast.

scenes.title: Lesson 12.1, on the balance sheet
scenes.result: Equity $280,000 · LTV 20% · health factor 4.0 · runway 7.6 months
scenes.vo: Here is the lesson twelve point one example, in order. Collateral of three hundred thousand, plus a reserve of forty thousand, is three hundred and forty thousand of assets. Loans are sixty thousand. Equity is three hundred and forty thousand minus sixty thousand, which is two hundred and eighty thousand. L.T.V. is sixty thousand divided by the collateral, which is twenty percent. The health factor is four point zero, and the reserve covers about seven point six months.
scenes.cap: Here is the lesson 12.1 example, in order. Collateral of $300,000, plus a reserve of $40,000, is $340,000 of assets. Loans are $60,000. Equity is $340,000 minus $60,000, which is $280,000. LTV is $60,000 divided by the collateral, which is 20%. The health factor is 4.0, and the reserve covers about 7.6 months.

scenes.label: On screen: the bank, the payout, the score

shots.caption: Read equity on the balance sheet

scenes.vo: On the balance sheet, equity reads two hundred and eighty thousand dollars. W eight reads that sheet and answers yes, because the health factor is above the floor. The income sheet, in the lesson thirteen point three example, shows a payout of sixteen thousand three hundred and ten dollars a year. On the risk register, a score of twenty means do not hold it until the response is real.
scenes.cap: On the balance sheet, equity reads $280,000. W8 reads that sheet and answers yes, because the health factor is above the floor. scenes.q: Collateral $300,000, reserve $40,000, loans $60,000. What is the equity?
scenes.a: $280,000. Add the reserve, then subtract the loans. A lesson example, not your book.
scenes.vo: Question one. The lesson balance sheet has three hundred thousand dollars of collateral, a forty thousand dollar reserve, and sixty thousand dollars of loans. What is the equity? [[pause 4]] The answer: two hundred and eighty thousand dollars. Add the reserve, then subtract the loans. This is a lesson example, not your book.
